title: One turn through OpenHands — step-by-step
example_input: fix the failing test in tests/test_auth.py
note: Representations below are simplified shapes of the real types at the pinned SHA, not verbatim dumps.

steps.title: Input
steps.narrative: The user sends 'fix the failing test in tests/test_auth.py'. LocalConversation.send_message() resets FINISHED/STUCK to IDLE, runs UserPromptSubmit hooks through HookEventProcessor.on_event — a deny blocks the message entirely — then matches skill triggers (get_user_message_suffix; matched names recorded in state.activated_knowledge_skills), and emits the user MessageEvent before entering run(). A blocked message surfaces in _step via state.pop_blocked_message -> FINISHED, so the hook veto lands before the model is ever consulted.
steps.representation:
send_message("fix the failing test in tests/test_auth.py")
  -> UserPromptSubmit hooks (HookEventProcessor.on_event)
     -> deny? block_message(id) ... _step: FINISHED, skip model
  -> get_user_message_suffix: KeywordTrigger / TaskTrigger / PathTrigger match
     -> skill content appended to user message
  -> MessageEvent(source="user") emitted on the stream

steps.title: Prompt assembly
steps.narrative: prepare_llm_messages(state.view, condenser, llm) builds the model input from the cached incremental view — the raw event list is never serialized directly. The system prompt carries AgentContext._resolve_dynamic_data() output, including the <available_skills> block listing every AgentSkills-format skill (descriptions truncated to 1024 chars per the AgentSkills spec). Tool declarations come from the registry: SDK builtins (finish, think, switch_llm, invoke_skill, ...) plus the default exec set (terminal, file_editor, task_tracker), resolved to implementations at runtime.
steps.representation:
prepare_llm_messages(
  view=state.view,          # cached, incrementally maintained
  condenser=condenser, llm=llm
)
  -> [SystemMessage(<available_skills>… 1024-char descs),
      MessageEvent…, ObservationEvent…, ActionEvent…]  # view invariants enforced

steps.title: Model call
steps.narrative: Agent._step calls llm.generate(messages, tools, add_security_risk_prediction=True, on_token=stream.token_callback). LLM is a frozen Pydantic model wrapping LiteLLM (litellm.completion/acompletion); it dispatches between Chat Completions and the Responses API per model (uses_responses_api). The add_security_risk_prediction flag asks the model to self-label each action's security risk — advisory input to the security analyzer, never a decision.
steps.representation:
llm.generate(
  messages, tools,
  add_security_risk_prediction=True,   # model self-labels action risk
  on_token=stream.token_callback       # StreamContext mints event IDs
)
  -> uses_responses_api() ? Responses API : Chat Completions
  -> LLMResponse

steps.title: Response parsing
steps.narrative: classify_response is a pure function — no side effects, no logging, no mutation. Decision priority, first match wins: TOOL_CALLS (message contains tool calls, e.g. terminal to run pytest, file_editor to view the test) > CONTENT (non-blank TextContent) > REASONING_ONLY (reasoning but no visible content) > EMPTY. Had the model answered in prose, CONTENT would emit a MessageEvent and finish the turn ('awaits user input'); reasoning-only or empty responses get a corrective nudge from source='environment' and the loop continues.
steps.representation:
classify_response(message)  # pure
  -> TOOL_CALLS      if message.tool_calls          # e.g. terminal, file_editor
  -> CONTENT        elif non-blank TextContent       # MessageEvent, FINISHED
  -> REASONING_ONLY elif reasoning, no content       # env nudge, continue
  -> EMPTY          else                            # env nudge, continue

steps.title: Tool dispatch
steps.narrative: _handle_tool_calls runs each call through _get_action_event: argument parsing -> normalize_tool_call (aliasing/terminal fallback) -> tool lookup -> Pydantic validation -> security-risk extraction -> critic evaluation — then emits the ActionEvent via on_event. As the event flows through HookEventProcessor, PreToolUse hooks fire; a deny marks the action blocked in state (state.block_action). Then the confirmation gate: _requires_user_confirmation checks the ConfirmationPolicy (AlwaysConfirm / NeverConfirm / ConfirmRisky) against per-action risks from the SecurityAnalyzerBase. Without a configured analyzer, risk is always UNKNOWN.
steps.representation:
_get_action_event(tool_call)
  1. parse args -> normalize_tool_call -> tool lookup
  2. Pydantic validation, security-risk extraction
  3. critic evaluation (_evaluate_with_critic) -> ActionEvent.critic_result
  -> on_event(ActionEvent) -> PreToolUse hooks may block_action(id)
  -> _requires_user_confirmation: policy x analyzer risk
     -> WAITING_FOR_CONFIRMATION, or proceed

steps.title: Feedback
steps.narrative: _execute_actions -> _ActionBatch.prepare: truncate the batch at FinishTool (later calls discarded), partition out hook-blocked actions (emitting UserRejectObservation with rejection_source='hook'), and execute the rest through ParallelToolExecutor bounded by tool_concurrency_limit — the async path runs each tool in its own thread (run_in_executor + asyncio.gather). ObservationEvents are emitted in original call order even though execution was parallel. A tool raising ValueError becomes an AgentErrorEvent so the model can self-correct.
steps.representation:
_ActionBatch.prepare()
  -> truncate at FinishTool (later calls discarded)
  -> partition hook-blocked -> UserRejectObservation(rejection_source="hook")
  -> ParallelToolExecutor: run_in_executor + asyncio.gather
     (bounded by tool_concurrency_limit, resource locking)
  -> ObservationEvent per call, in ORIGINAL call order

steps.title: Termination
steps.narrative: Say the model then calls finish. _ActionBatch.finalize runs the iterative-refinement check: if the critic scores the work below threshold, a followup prompt is injected as a user-role message and the loop continues; otherwise status flips to FINISHED. Back in _run, the Stop hooks get their word — a deny flips FINISHED back to RUNNING with the feedback injected as an environment message — and only then does the loop break.
steps.representation:
finish -> _ActionBatch.finalize()
  -> check_iterative_refinement: score < threshold?
     yes -> inject followup user MessageEvent, loop continues
     no  -> FINISHED
  -> _run: run_stop(reason="agent_finished")
     deny -> FINISHED flips back to RUNNING + env feedback
  -> break

steps.title: Rendering
steps.narrative: Every event emitted through on_event fans out: the EventLog appends it as JSONL under the conversation directory (thread/process-safe), and in server mode the EventService publishes it over pub/sub to REST/WebSocket clients, with StreamContext minting event IDs so streaming slots can be retired. There is no privileged renderer — the TUI, the web client, and the TypeScript client all consume the same event stream.
steps.representation:
on_event(event)
  -> EventLog: append JSONL (thread/process-safe, FileStore locking)
  -> EventService: pub/sub -> REST / WebSocket clients
  -> StreamContext: minted event IDs retire streaming slots
// no privileged renderer — TUI, web, TS client share one stream
